descripcion: Many near-synonyms in English carry a positive, neutral or negative connotation that a dictionary definition doesn't show: slim vs. skinny, confident vs. arrogant, frugal vs. stingy. Choosing the wrong one changes how the listener feels about the person or thing being described, even though the literal meaning is close to identical.

ejemplos.texto: She comes across as confident, not arrogant, which is a hard balance to strike.
He's frugal rather than stingy — there's a real difference.
It's more curiosity than nosiness, in my view.

notas: Connotation often depends on who is being described and by whom — the same behaviour can be called confident or arrogant depending on the speaker's attitude.
Swapping a neutral word for a loaded one is a subtle but powerful way to shift a reader's sympathy without stating an opinion directly.
These pairs are worth learning together, not in isolation, since the contrast is the whole point.

es.en: Spanish has similar connotation pairs (ahorrativo/tacaño, seguro/soberbio), so the concept is familiar. The difficulty is that specific words do not always sit on the same axis: English frugal is more neutral-positive than its closest Spanish translation.
es.es: El español tiene pares de connotación similares («ahorrativo/tacaño», «seguro/soberbio»), por lo que el concepto es familiar. La dificultad es que las palabras concretas no siempre ocupan el mismo punto del eje: «frugal» en inglés es más neutro-positivo que su traducción española más cercana.

de.en: English and German share many parallel pairs (thrifty/stingy – sparsam/geizig, slim/skinny – schlank/dürr), so the concept transfers well. Sensibel is a false friend, however: it means sensitive, not sensible.
de.de: Englisch und Deutsch teilen viele parallele Paare («thrifty/stingy» – «sparsam/geizig», «slim/skinny» – «schlank/dürr»), daher ist das Konzept vertraut. «Sensibel» ist jedoch ein falscher Freund: Es bedeutet «sensitive», nicht «sensible».

it.en: Italian frugale mostly describes a simple meal, while English frugal describes careful spending. Italian speakers therefore need to learn frugal as a money word with a neutral-positive tone.
it.it: In italiano «frugale» descrive soprattutto un pasto semplice, mentre in inglese «frugal» indica attenzione alle spese. Gli italofoni devono quindi imparare «frugal» come parola legata al denaro con tono neutro-positivo.

fr.en: French frugal mostly describes a simple meal or lifestyle, while English frugal describes careful spending. French speakers therefore need to learn frugal as a money word with a neutral-positive tone.
fr.fr: En français, «frugal» décrit surtout un repas ou un mode de vie simple, tandis qu'en anglais «frugal» concerne la gestion économe de l'argent. Les francophones doivent donc apprendre ce mot anglais comme un terme financier à connotation neutre-positive.

pt.en: Portuguese frugal mostly describes a simple meal, while English frugal describes careful spending. Portuguese speakers need to learn frugal as a money word with a neutral-positive tone.
pt.pt: Em português, «frugal» costuma descrever sobretudo uma refeição simples, enquanto em inglês «frugal» descreve cuidado com gastos. Falantes de português precisam aprender «frugal» como uma palavra ligada a dinheiro, com tom neutro-positivo.

errores: Choosing a negatively connotated word when a neutral or positive one was intended.
Not noticing that a supposedly neutral translation actually carries a stronger judgement in English.
Overcorrecting into an unnaturally positive word to avoid any negative connotation, which can sound insincere.

traducciones.pt: Isso é dizer de forma suave.

redemittel.expresion: That word does more damage than you intend.

traducciones.es: Esa palabra hace más daño del que querés.
traducciones.de: Dieses Wort richtet mehr Schaden an, als du willst.
traducciones.fr: Ce mot fait plus de dégâts que tu ne le veux.
traducciones.it: Quella parola fa più danni di quanto intendi.
traducciones.pt: Essa palavra faz mais estragos do que queres.

redemittel.expresion: Which of the two do you actually mean?
redemittel.funcion: forces the connotation choice into the open

traducciones.es: ¿Cuál de las dos querés decir en realidad?
traducciones.de: Welches von beiden meinst du eigentlich?
traducciones.fr: Lequel des deux veux-tu dire au juste ?
traducciones.pt: Qual dos dois queres dizer realmente?

autochequeo: Does each word carry the connotation I actually intend?
Have I checked a near-synonym for hidden negative or positive charge?
Would the described person feel fairly represented by this word choice?
Have I avoided overcorrecting into an insincerely positive word?
Are at least four connotation pairs used deliberately?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on connotation. Flag any word that carries an unintended positive or negative charge and suggest the neutral or opposite-charge alternative. Do not rewrite the text.
